questions.q: Why does this lesson argue that a data quality issue needs to be formally tracked rather than just mentioned informally?
options: An untracked issue has no owner, no priority, no due date, and no way to confirm months later that it was actually fixed
Formal tracking is only required by certain government regulations
Informal mentions are always more accurate than tracked records
Tracking is only needed for issues with zero business impact
questions.explain: Issue management turns a one-time mention into something trackable and closeable.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the fields a well-formed issue record should include, per this lesson?
options: The CEO's personal approval signature
Severity
Owner
Status
questions.explain: The lesson lists description, affected table/field, detected by, severity, owner, root cause, status, and due date — not an executive signature.

questions.q: What distinguishes the "verified" stage from the "resolved" stage in the issue lifecycle?
options: Resolved means a fix was applied; verified means the original detection check was re-run and confirmed passing
They are the same stage with two different names
Verified comes before resolved in the lifecycle
Verified only applies to manually fixed issues, never automated ones
questions.explain: Jumping from resolved straight to closed without verifying is the same risky shortcut Lesson 25 warned about for remediation.

questions.q: According to this lesson, which factor should influence how open issues get prioritized?
options: Blast radius — how many downstream reports a single root cause actually affects
Whichever issue was logged first, strictly in order received
Alphabetical order of the affected table name
Whichever team complains the loudest, regardless of impact
questions.explain: The lesson names business impact, blast radius, severity, and fixability as prioritization factors — not arrival order or volume of complaints.

questions.q: How does issue management connect to monitoring and root cause analysis from earlier in this chapter?
options: Monitoring detects and creates the issue, root cause analysis fills in its cause field, and remediation moves its status toward resolved and then verified
Issue management replaces the need for monitoring entirely
Root cause analysis and issue management are unrelated processes
Issues can only be created manually, never from an automated monitor
questions.explain: Issue management is the record-keeping layer that ties monitoring, root cause work, and remediation together into one accountable loop.
